sections.overview: The Gulf wobbegong is a large, bottom-dwelling carpet shark of southern Australian coastal and shelf waters.
sections.identification: It has dark-edged brown saddles and fewer pale rings than the spotted wobbegong; it is larger than the similar ornate wobbegong.
sections.habitat: It rests among reef caves and ledges, in bays and on rocky or coral reefs, and ranges from inshore waters onto the continental shelf.
sections.diet: A stomach-content study in New South Wales found a diet mainly of bony fishes, with cephalopods and other sharks also recorded.
sections.behavior: It rests on the seabed by day and makes nocturnal excursions from its resting places.
sections.reproduction: It is live-bearing, but litter-size and timing data are better established for its close relative O. ornatus than for this species.
sections.ecology: Once treated as O. ornatus, it is now recognized as a distinct species; the two profiles compare the larger Gulf wobbegong with the smaller ornate wobbegong.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern; Australian fisheries reporting nevertheless tracks catches and management.
